title: Prudential Regulation Authority Business Plan 2026/27
summary: The PRA published its 2026/27 Business Plan outlining supervisory priorities including embedding liquidity reporting for insurers, implementing Basel III rules finalized in January 2026, finalizing a simplified capital regime for small domestic banks effective January 2027, and taking forward ring-fencing reforms in coordination with HM Treasury. The document is primarily an administrative planning document that summarizes already-announced regulatory initiatives rather than introducing new market-moving policies.
key_points: Basel III remaining elements finalized and published in January 2026, with implementation proceeding through 2026/27; stated not to increase overall capital requirements
Simplified capital regime for small domestic banks finalized, fully effective from January 2027
PRA regulates 1,254 firms: 686 deposit-takers and 568 insurers of all types
Bank liquidity supervisory work being taken forward in response to faster bank runs experienced mainly in US in 2023
Headcount reduction of approximately 140 staff planned to generate savings for systems investment
Periodic Summary Meetings moving to a two-year cycle for all firms
Operational incident and third-party relationship reporting requirements being implemented jointly with FCA
Chief Executive Sam Woods' term concluding in June 2026, to be succeeded by Katharine Braddick
why_it_matters: This business plan provides an overview of UK prudential regulatory trajectory for the coming year. While it largely summarizes existing initiatives rather than introducing new policies, it signals continued PRA focus on bank and insurer resilience, Basel III implementation completion, and operational resilience. The ring-fencing regime reforms and work on insurer liquidity requirements could have indirect implications for how financial institutions structure their operations and manage liquidity risk.
